title: Extension by zero through the schematic closure
statement:
In the situation of [det-nagata-density-normalization-setup], let
$\Lambda$ be a condensed coefficient ring with pulled-back coefficient
sheaves $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Z,\Lambda_{\overline X}$. For every sheaf $M$ of
$\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}}$ the unit
$\eta:j_!M\to i_*i^*j_!M$ of $i^*\dashv i_*$ is an isomorphism, and the
base-change isomorphism $i^*j_!M\simeq j_{Z,!}M$ identifies it with a natural
isomorphism

$$
j_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }i_*j_{Z,!}M .
$$

Consequently, for every complex $K$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules (unbounded), the
same map, applied degreewise, is an isomorphism of complexes
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$, and it induces the identification
$j_!K\simeq i_*j_{Z,!}K$ in $D(\overline X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}},\Lambda_{\overline X})$.

proof.text: Use the canonical image factorization j_Z ; i = j and the complementary open V from the setup. Noetherianity makes this open complement quasi-compact. The range of j lies in the range of i, so its intersection with V is empty. The square (id_X,j_Z,j,i) is Cartesian because i is a monomorphism: IsPullback.of_horiz_isIso_mono supplies its universal property.

source.place: Steps 1 and 3: the complementary open and the Cartesian image square

proof.text: The existing abelian extension-by-zero vanishing theorem makes j_V^* j_! M zero on underlying abelian sheaves. Apply abelian_closed_support to the complementary pair (i,j_V). This proves that the specified abelian closed unit at j_! M is invertible. On underlying sheaves the specified internal module unit is the abelian unit followed by i_* of the scalar-extension unit. The scalar-extension unit is invertible because alpha_i is an isomorphism: composing it with extendScalarsIsoComapInv is the identity. The module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so the original specified module unit is invertible. This is the private supportedUnit helper, and proves the first clause without changing either adjunction.

source.place: Steps 3 and 4: vanishing and the actual supported closed unit

proof.text: For a Cartesian open square, the existing abelian open-extension base-change isomorphism identifies the underlying sheaf of g^* j_! M with an object in the image of jprime_!. This abelian isomorphism is the conjugate of weakly-etale base change under the composite adjunctions. The open counit is therefore invertible on that underlying sheaf. The counit of the linearized open adjunction has precisely that underlying map, so is invertible since forgetting reflects isomorphisms. Restriction and coextension along the invertible coefficient map form an equivalence, so its counit is invertible too. Expanding the specified module open adjunction shows that its counit on g^* j_! M is a composite of these invertible maps. The private cartesianCounit helper proves this. Similarly linearization of the fully faithful abelian open extension, followed by the coefficient restriction equivalence, is fully faithful; thus the specified module open unit is invertible (private openUnit).

source.place: Step 2: base change used to detect the essential image

proof.text: Let t be the original open unit followed by nagataClosurePullbackComparison, as in the required formula. Define alpha componentwise as precisely the transpose displayed in the theorem. Apply the injective adjunction Hom bijection and its left and right naturality equations to reduce naturality of alpha to naturality of t. The private comparisonOfUnits theorem performs this construction for abstract adjunctions, so elaboration does not unfold the large sheaf-operation definitions. Adjunction.homEquiv_counit expresses alpha_M as j_Z,! applied to t_M followed by the open counit. The original open unit and pullback-composition map are invertible, and the counit at i^* j_! M is invertible by the preceding Cartesian argument, so alpha is a natural isomorphism. Set beta = alpha^{-1}. No equality between an arbitrary comparison and the normalized map is assumed.

source.place: Step 2: the explicitly normalized inverse base-change map

proof.text: Whisker the actual closed unit with j_! and convert it to an isomorphism using its proved components. Compose it with i_* of beta. The resulting theta has exactly the component formula in the statement, definitionally. Apply NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex to this natural isomorphism, and then DerivedCategory.Q.map to each component. Both preserve isomorphisms. These are the very maps in the assertion; no boundedness is used. The stated derived clause is the image of a particular chain map under Q, so it does not require constructing or comparing descended derived functors.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1–5; direct lift of the existing abelian support and Cartesian essential-image results, with the original unit/counit-normalized maps. N1, 2026-10-21.
